standards.mechanism: Guard as a Claude Code PreToolUse command hook: hook JSON on stdin (tool_name, tool_input.command, agent_type for a subagent), permissionDecision deny or ask, no output for no decision
Force-push forms the guard denies: -f, --force, --force-with-lease, --force-if-includes, --mirror, + refspec
gh api writes: -X/--method, and -f/-F/--raw-field/--input implying POST
Workflow triggers: pull_request plus push filtered to main (on.push.branches)
GitHub flow: every change on a branch, merged through its pull request
Ref lookup on origin with git ls-remote --exit-code --heads and the full ref name
Hook JSON built with jq --arg (no shell quoting of the command)
Guard cases for bash line continuation: a backslash-newline pair is removed before words are read
Guard cases for quoted and escaped words: bash removes quotes and backslashes before the command sees its arguments
Guard cases for git option abbreviations (an unambiguous long-option prefix is accepted)
Guard cases for command substitution: $( ) and backticks run a command whose output becomes part of a word, so its words are not readable from the text; the guard fails closed on them
Guard cases for gh's command aliases (pr new, secret remove, variable remove, pr ls, ...)

The guard reads each simple command as shell words with Python's shlex in POSIX mode (punctuation_chars for ( ) ; & | < > and the newline); forms shlex does not model (ANSI-C or locale quoting, a quoted or escaped lone separator, brace expansion, an unbalanced quote) make the command unreadable, which fails closed when it names git or gh
Guard cases for process substitution <( ) and >( ), which runs a command as $( ) does

A redirection (its operator, its target word and the file descriptor number before it) is not one of the command's arguments, so the guard drops it before reading the words; >| is a redirection, not a pipe
A shell reads its commands from standard input with -s, or when no operand follows its options (-o and -O take a value), so such a shell fails closed
The same for bash: -c reads the command string, -s or no operand reads standard input; --rcfile and --init-file take a value
A pipe connects one command's output to the next command's standard input, so text echoed into a shell is run by it
A here-string (<<<) and a heredoc feed their text to the command's standard input
`.` and `source` read and run a file's commands, so of /dev/stdin they run standard input
git's global option --attr-source <tree-ish> takes the next word as its value

--- a/AGENTS.md

@@ -91,7 +91,7 @@
 - **Branches.** A story is built and committed on `feature/<story>` (`<story>` matching `^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+[a-z]?$`). Any other change (a records change, a Small fix, a docs-only change) goes on `feature/<slug>` (`<slug>` matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9.-]{0,49}$`, so it never matches a story ID). Both take the same steps and wait for the full checks: every check job, the e2e journeys and the ZAP baseline included, runs on every pull request and on main.
 - **Steps** (the commands are in `docs/process/agentic-sdlc.md`, section 2). Push the branch; open its pull request against main, or against `feature/<base>` for a stacked story, titled with the commit-message subject (one line, at most 72 characters) and with the detail in the body, which becomes the squash commit's message; wait for its required checks. Only once every stage has passed and the base reads main, arm squash auto-merge pinned to the head whose tree the stages checked (`--match-head-commit`); auto-merge never replaces a stage. Before any later push to an armed pull request, disable auto-merge, and re-arm on the new head once its checks pass. Then confirm the merge and its squash commit, and wait for main's CI and Security runs on that commit. Every `gh` write and read-back runs as the repository owner (`GH_TOKEN="$(gh auth token --user <owner>)" gh …`); the token is never printed, logged or written to a file.
 - **What main gets.** Main takes only a squash merge. The pull request's checks test GitHub's merge of the up-to-date branch into main, and main's own run builds, scans and publishes the squash commit (ad-012). A pull request that is only behind main is updated with `gh pr update-branch`, never a force push; one with a conflict, or a drift check that fails after an update, goes to a builder as a fix round, since the supervisor writes no code.
-- **Stacked stories.** A story that depends on an unmerged story builds on that story's branch, `feature/<base>`, and opens its pull request against it. When the base squash-merges, GitHub deletes `feature/<base>` and retargets the stacked pull request to main; the stacked branch is rebased onto main (`git rebase --onto origin/main <base's last head> feature/<story>`), pushed with the one lease-checked force push, `git [-C <path>] push --force-with-lease --force-if-includes origin feature/<story>`, and its checks run again before any merge. No other force push is made; main is never force-pushed, and the ruleset refuses it.
+- **Stacked stories.** A story that depends on an unmerged story builds on that story's branch, `feature/<base>`, and opens its pull request against it. When the base squash-merges, GitHub deletes `feature/<base>` and retargets the stacked pull request to main; the stacked branch is rebased onto main (`git rebase --onto origin/main <base's last head> feature/<story>`), pushed with the one lease-checked force push, `git [-C <path>] push --force-with-lease --force-if-includes origin feature/<story>`, and its checks run again before any merge. No other force push is made; main is force-pushed only by the supervisor.
 - **Records.** The records of a merged story (the capture, the epic's lows and decisions, a stage's read-back record, and the story's `docs/tickets/README.md` row set to `done`) ride in one records pull request, `feature/records-<story>`, after its merge.
